title: C482/1852/2018 of MAHENDRA SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No. 1852 of 2018
(Under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.)
Mahendra Singh ... Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ... Respondents
Advocate: Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate, for the applicant.
Mr. Subhash Tyagi Bhardwaj, Deputy Advocate General, along
with Mr. Balvinder Singh Thind, Brief Holder, for the State
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
An FIR, being FIR No. 18 of 2018, dated 20th
January 2018 was registered by Sabir Hussain i.e. the
complainant herein, contending thereof, that an
agreement for sale dated 7th February 2006, was
registered by the present applicant for sale of land,
lying in khasra No. 147, situated in Jaspur Patti,
Tirmal, district Udham Singh Nagar. Owing to the fact,
that despite of agreement for sale dated 7th February
2006, no sale deed was executed, hence he has
already instituted a Suit for specific performance, and
since the applicant was contemplating to further
execute the sale deed or enter into an agreement for
sale in favour of other persons, other than the
complainant of the FIR, the complainant has alleged,
that as against the agreement for sale dated 7th
February 2006, he has already availed certain financial
assistance from the Allahabad bank, but due to denial
of execution of the sale deed, the complainant has
submitted, that the applicant has committed an offence
under Section 420 of IPC.

2
2. The investigation was conducted by the officer
concerned, and the Chargesheet had been submitted
against the present applicant, being Chargesheet No.
49 of 2018 dated 28th March 2018, on which the
cognizance have been taken, resulting into registration
of Criminal Case No. 483 of 2018, State Vs. Mahendra
Singh, whereby the applicant has been summoned to
be tried for the aforesaid offence.
3. When this C482 Application was instituted before
the Registry of this Court on 20th November 2018, it
was heard by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court and
the coordinate Bench of this Court, after considering
the fact that the controversy is arising out of an alleged
agreement for sale dated 7th February 2006, and since
coupled with the fact, there was already a pending Suit
for specific performance, the Court proceeded to grant
an interim order dated 22nd November 2018, and the
notices were issued to respondent No. 3. Steps have
been taken and there is an office report that
respondent No. 3, has been served with the notices,
but till date none has put in appearance on his behalf.
4. At the subsequent stage, the learned counsel for
the applicant had filed the supplementary affidavit
wherein he had placed on record the judgment, which
has been rendered by the Civil Judge (Senior Division),
Kashipur, district Udham Singh Nagar, in Civil Suit No.
8 of 2010, Sabir Hussain (complainant) Vs. Mahendra
Singh (applicant).

3
5. The said Civil Suit for specific performance of the
applicant has been decreed partially by the judgement
dated 25th March 2019. As per the directions contained
in the judgement dated 25th March 2019, the applicant
had been directed to remit back the partial sale
consideration, which was received by him in pursuance
to the agreement for sale dated 7th February 2006.
6. In that eventuality, the interse dispute between
the parties has decided by the Court of Civil Judge
(Senior Division), Kashipur, district Udham Singh
Nagar, by the judgement and decree dated 25th March
2019, and if at all the complainant has got any
grievances, as against the judgement and decree dated
25th March 2019, it would be open for him to resort to
an appropriate resource available to him on a civil side
by putting a challenge to the judgment and decree
before the Appellate Forum under Section 96 of CPC.
7. But so far as the controversy pertaining to the
commission of offence under Section 420 of IPC, which
was complained of in the FIR, on account of non
execution of the sale deed in pursuance to the
agreement for sale dated 7th February 2006, that issue
no more is available to the complainant to be
adjudicated on merits, as now the parties will have to
litigate before the Civil Appellate Forum for redressal of
their grievances.

4
8. In view of the aforesaid, the present C482
Application would stand allowed; as a consequence
thereto, the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 483 of
2018, State Vs. Mahendra Singh, would hereby stand
dropped; but, however, dropping of the proceedings
will not have any bearing or an adverse affect on the
rights of the complainant, in case, if he chooses to
prefer an Appeal against the judgement and decree
rendered in a Suit for specific performance.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 06.12.2022
Mahinder/
